elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 13.4 as rendered: "each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed the fees paid or payable to M&I by Customer ..." — the former M&I-only cap is now bilateral, and no retained sentence states Customer's liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: The rendered cap is a single-limb "fees paid or payable ... during the twelve (12) months prior to the event" with no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor; the temporal anchor is also "prior to the event" rather than preceding the claim. To reach preferred, insert "the greater of (a) ... and (b) USD 1,000,000".

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 13.2: "Neither Customer nor M&I shall be liable for ... any indirect, incidental, punitive, special or consequential damages ..." — mutual and unchanged.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The limitation of liability in the first sentence of this Section 13.4 shall not apply to ... breach of its confidentiality obligations under Section 17 ..."

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: The added carve-out sentence lists only indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and willful misconduct; no data protection or security obligations are named. Add "breach of its data protection or security obligations" to the carve-out list for preferred.
Added sentence expressly disapplies the cap to "a party's indemnification obligations under Section 14.2".
Fraud is absent from the carve-out sentence; add "fraud" to the Excluded Claims list for the preferred level.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears in the rendered Section 13.4 sentence; add "infringement of the other party's intellectual property rights".

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: The only collection language is the retained proviso attached to the one-year suit limitation ("the foregoing limitation shall not apply to the collection of any amounts due"), which qualifies the time bar, not the liability cap; no statement excludes Customer's payment obligations from capped damages.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: "each party's total liability under this Agreement shall not exceed ..." — cap is expressly mutual.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: "the fees paid or payable to M&I by Customer under this Agreement during the twelve (12) months prior to the event" — twelve months of fees, replacing the three-month payments basis.
Carve-out sentence: cap "shall not apply to a party's indemnification obligations under Section 14.2", placing indemnities outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Carve-out sentence covers "breach of its confidentiality obligations under Section 17".

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the edited first sentence of Section 13.4 makes the cap mutual ("each party's total liability") and moves the basis from three months' payments to twelve months' fees paid or payable, and the single added sentence places indemnification (Section 14.2), confidentiality (Section 17), gross negligence and willful misconduct outside the cap.

Preferred fails on five elements: no greater-of USD 1,000,000 floor (and the anchor remains "prior to the event" rather than preceding the claim), and no carve-outs for data protection/security obligations, fraud, or infringement of the other party's IP; Customer's payment obligations are still not excluded from capped damages — the retained "collection of any amounts due" proviso qualifies only the one-year suit limitation.

Minimality holds: the drafter edited the existing cap sentence in place, retained the one-year action limitation and its collection proviso, retained the mutual Section 13.2 exclusion unchanged, and added exactly the carve-outs required by the fallback checklist with no survival tail, expense language, procedures or extra damages categories.

Intent is preserved: the "Notwithstanding any provision in this Agreement" opener, the time-bar sentence, and the cross-references to Sections 14.2 and 17 survive without contradiction, and no defined term or cross-reference is left dangling.

Deviation classification is correct: the original clause capped only M&I at three months' payments (below the six-month walk-away floor) with indemnities inside the cap, so the fallback was not met on material terms before the edit.
